body.input: Which companies opened an office in Norway in 2026?

response.content:
I was unable to find a comprehensive, definitive list of all companies that opened an office in Norway in 2026. However, based on available information, here are some notable developments:

- **Folketrygdfondet (State Fund in Tromsø)** — The Norwegian State Fund opened a new office in Tromsø, Northern Norway, in 2026. The office, located in the former Mack brewery premises, was officially opened by Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg. The fund will invest in Nordic small-cap listed companies.

- **Data centre operators** — Norway has seen significant interest from data centre companies (including existing presences from **Microsoft**, **Nscale**, **TikTok** (via Green Mountain), and **CoreWeave**), though the Norwegian government temporarily halted new data centre grid connections in 2026 to manage controlled growth until regulations are in place (expected at least until August 2027).

Many large multinational companies maintain an operational presence in Norway (including ConocoPhillips, BP, Tesla, Dell Technologies, Booking Holdings, BAE Systems, Aon, Marsh & McLennan, and others), but these are long-standing presences rather than new 2026 office openings.

For a complete picture of all companies that opened new offices in Norway during 2026, you may want to consult the Norwegian business register (Brønnøysundregistrene) or Innovation Norway's investment records, which track new foreign direct investments and company registrations in real time.

explainability.content: The State Fund managed by Folketrygdfondet opened a new office in Tromsø, Northern Norway, in 2026, as documented by the official opening ceremony with Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg.

Data centre operators such as Microsoft, Nscale, TikTok (via Green Mountain), and CoreWeave are mentioned as existing presences in Norway, but the source indicates a government pause on new data centre developments in 2026, implying no new office openings for these firms that year.

The extensive list of companies with operational presence in Norway (e.g., ConocoPhillips, BP, Tesla, Dell Technologies, Booking Holdings, etc.) reflects long‑standing operations rather than new 2026 openings, supporting the answer’s distinction between existing presences and the only confirmed new office in 2026.

# Opened State Fund in Tromsø, Northern Norway

Statens fond i Tromsø, som forvaltes av Folketrygdfondet, skal snart i gang med sine investeringer. Kontoret i de tidligere lokalene til Mack ølbryggeri ble offisielt åpnet mandag av finansminister Jens Stoltenberg (Ap) sammen med tidligere finansminister Trygve Slagsvold Vedum (Sp) og Tromsø-ordfører Gunnar Wilhelmsen. (Foto: Astri Edvardsen) [...] The State Fund in Tromsø, managed by Folketrygdfondet, will soon start investing. Its office in the city center was officially opened on Monday by Norway's Minister of Finance Jens Stoltenberg (Labor) together with the former MoF and now MP Trygve Slagsvold Vedum (Centre), and Tromsø Mayor Gunnar Wilhelmsen.

 

Astri Edvardsen [...] · Swedish companies account for around half of the fund's investment universe, followed by Danish (22 percent), Finnish (13 percent), Norwegian (9 percent), and Icelandic (6 percent) companies. The three largest sectors will be industry (27 percent), health (25 percent), and finance (21 percent).

The announcement will pause any new data center developments - but any projects already approved for a grid connection, or those already connected, will be unaffected.

Norway has become a popular location for new data centers, and Statnett said it expects the restrictions to be in place until at least August 2027, as fluctuating data center loads could destabilize grid operations across the country.

Norway says no more new data centers for the time being

Norwegian flag

Norway has temporarily halted the building of new data centers in the country as it looks to limit the fast roll-out of new AI facilities.

System operator Statnett and the Norwegian government confirmed the move will look to halt the rapid expansion of power-intensive data centers across the country until regulations are in place. [...] However around 18GW is currently being requested for connection - over a third of the country's peak power demand.

Norway has already imposed a temporary ban on the establishment of new data centers used to mine cryptocurrencies, and is already the site of existing and planned data centers from big players such as Microsoft, Nscale, TikTok (through Green Mountain), and CoreWeave.
